sections.h2: Which Early County office do you call about a tax bill?
sections.html:
The Early County Assessor handles valuation, while the tax commissioner handles the bill itself. The county's forms and applications page carries a Tax Commissioner Forms link. The assessor's number is (229) 723-3088. For anything else, the county administration building at 204 Court Square in Blakely answers at (229) 723-4304 on weekdays, closing for lunch at noon and reopening at 1:00 p.m. until 5:00 p.m.

Parcel records are on qPublic under the Early County listing. State guidance sends payment questions, homestead applications and bill copies to the commissioner, and sends appeals and appraised value questions to the assessor.

  • Appraised value, property record or appeal: the assessor.
  • Bill copy, payment or homestead form: the tax commissioner.
  • Unsure where a form belongs: the administration office in Blakely.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about Early County itself?
sections.html:
Four cities sit inside the county: Blakely, the seat, plus Damascus, Jakin and Arlington, which Early shares with Calhoun County. Georgia formed Early County in 1818 from land obtained from the Creek Indians. Eight later counties, including Dougherty, Grady, Miller, Mitchell and Seminole, were cut from its original territory.

Peanut farming drives local income. The county's history page describes Early as the largest peanut quota holding county in the nation, and a peanut statue went up on the Blakely square in 1954. Kolomoki Mounds State Park, in the north central part, preserves a row of Native American mounds from around the year 800, with a museum covering the area's cultural history since about 5000 B.C. The Early County Museum and the Coheelee Creek Covered Bridge are the other listed attractions.

Census figures show a typical owned home worth $131,300 among 4,993 housing units, and only 12 building permits in 2025. New construction barely registers here.

The county website also lists a code enforcement page, a code of ordinances on Municode, an airport, the Blakely-Early County Recreation Department and a UGA Extension office. Look at the code enforcement page and the ordinances if your house has sat vacant, since a seller who clears any open issues first gives a buyer fewer reasons to hesitate.

sections.h2: What do Early County appraisal visits and notices involve?
sections.html:
Appraisers may turn up at your parcel in any month. The county's standing notice cites O.C.G.A. 48-5-264.1 and names the triggers: a return, an appeal, a site improvement permit, a homestead or conservation use application, or a routine review. Keep permit paperwork for any addition you built, since the county's forms page lists building, electrical and manufactured home permits. Staff collect only necessary details and photographs, and they leave a business card at an empty house. A visitor should show photo ID and arrive in a marked vehicle, and a call to the assessor settles any doubt.

It also points out that older owners can claim additional exemptions beyond the regular homestead one, with April 1 as the last day to apply. The full law behind each exemption controls eligibility.

A state revenue briefing from May 2026 outlines a redesigned Notice of Assessment under SB 566. Under that outline the notice lists exemptions and credits, estimates tax savings, names an appeal contact, spells out fair market value and says a homestead application may still be filed inside the 45-day appeal window. It also asks owners who are ineligible for a homestead exemption to say so before the window closes, because the tax and a 50 percent penalty stay with the property.

sections.h2: How do Early County appeals and homestead filings work?
sections.html:
An owner who disputes a value writes to the Early County Assessor within 45 days of the notice's mailing date. The statewide appeal form lets you challenge taxability, value, uniformity or a refused exemption, and you choose a Board of Equalization, a hearing officer or an arbitrator on it.

Nobody at the state level can overrule the local decision makers on one parcel's value, whether that is the assessors, a Board of Equalization, a hearing officer, an arbitrator or Superior Court. The state treats assessed value as 40 percent of fair market value, and the formula deducts the homestead exemption from that assessed figure before the millage rate applies.

That briefing also reports that the 2026 HOME Act ends the local opt-out from the HB 581 floating homestead exemption. The statewide version takes effect January 1, 2027 with 2026 values as its baseline, so a 2026 value carries weight beyond one tax year.

A homestead claim requires title and residence on January 1. File with the tax commissioner, or with the assessor in counties that delegate it, by the April 1 return deadline or during the 45-day appeal window. Before filing, do the following:

  • Save the notice and mark its mailing date.
  • Photograph defects and collect repair bids that support a lower value.
  • Request the property record card from the assessor and compare its square footage and condition notes with the house.
  • Ask which local exemptions Early County adds to the state's $2,000 standard exemption.

sections.h2: What do the Early County numbers look like?
sections.html:
Early is thinly settled: about 21 residents per square mile across 512.6 square miles of land. Its 10,455 estimated residents in mid-2025 are 3.7 percent fewer than the 2020 base, and older adults make up 22.6 percent of the total, which makes the age-based exemptions especially relevant.

Owners with no mortgage report typical monthly costs of $477, and about 14.7 percent of adults 25 and older hold a bachelor's degree. Rental housing is modest too, at a typical $791 a month. An heir or older owner preparing to sell should look for unpaid tax and budget for repairs.

sections.h2: What does an Early County seller owe in tax at closing?
sections.html:
Georgia charges the full year to whoever owned the parcel on January 1 and, per the state's FAQ, gives nothing back for a later sale. Most counties allow 60 days to pay with a normal due date of December 20, though local dates vary. The Early County tax commissioner can tell you the billing date and your parcel's balance.

Before signing a sale contract, ask the commissioner for a payoff number and whether any earlier years are still open. Liens issued by the commissioner are dealt with through that office. Filed liens appear on the clerk's general execution docket, so the clerk's index is worth a look as well.

Some Early County owners choose a no-repair cash sale for a house with a worn roof, tenants or back taxes, since the buyer absorbs the repairs and the balance is paid from proceeds.

faqs.q: Which office sets values in Early County?
faqs.a: The Early County Assessor, reachable at (229) 723-3088, sets values and takes appeals. The tax commissioner bills and collects.

faqs.q: May Early County appraisers drop by unannounced?
faqs.a: Yes. A standing county notice allows visits all year for returns, appeals, permits, exemption applications or routine review. Staff show photo ID, use a marked vehicle and leave a card at an empty house.

faqs.q: What is the filing window for an Early County assessment appeal?
faqs.a: Forty-five days from the notice's mailing date. Write to the assessor and name your route: Board of Equalization, hearing officer or arbitrator.

faqs.q: What is the deadline for an Early County homestead exemption?
faqs.a: April 1 for the current year, or the 45-day appeal window after a notice. You must have owned and lived in the house on January 1.

faqs.q: If I sell in spring, is the Early County tax bill still mine?
faqs.a: Yes. The January 1 owner is responsible for the year, and Georgia gives no partial-year refund. Get the balance from the tax commissioner and settle it at closing.
